record.original_question: For a closed surface Σ_g of genus g > 1 equipped with a real flat projective structure, Choi's theorem gives a unique decomposition along disjoint simple closed geodesics into pieces that are either annuli covered by an affine half-space or interiors of compact convex real flat projective surfaces with negative Euler characteristic. Is there an analogous decomposition or classification theorem in the 3-dimensional real flat projective case?

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.1. Let g>1 and suppose Σ_g has a real flat projective structure, then there exists a collection of disjoint simple closed geodesics C_1,\dots, C_k on Σ_g such that Σ_g/\cup C_i consists of an annulus covered by an affine half-space; the interior of a compact convex real flat projective surface with negative Euler characteristic. Furthermore, each C_i bounds either one or two annuli. Such a decomposition is unique.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A real flat projective structure (also called a real projective structure) on a manifold M^n is a maximal atlas of charts to RP^n whose transition maps are restrictions of projective transformations in PGL(n+1, R). For a closed surface Σ_g of genus g > 1 carrying such a structure, the following decomposition theorem holds: there exists a (possibly empty) collection of pairwise disjoint simple closed geodesics C_1, …, C_k on Σ_g such that each connected component of Σ_g \ (C_1 ∪ … ∪ C_k) is either

(i) an annulus that is projectively covered by an affine half-space (an "elementary" annulus), or

(ii) the interior of a compact convex real projective surface with negative Euler characteristic (where a real projective surface is convex if its developing map is a diffeomorphism onto a properly convex domain in RP^2).

Moreover each curve C_i bounds either one or two annuli of type (i), and such a decomposition is unique.

Problem. Formulate and prove a 3-dimensional analogue of this theorem. Precisely: given a closed 3-manifold M^3 equipped with a real flat projective structure, find a canonical decomposition of M^3 along a finite collection of disjoint embedded surfaces (totally geodesic, or otherwise canonically defined) into pieces falling into an explicit finite list of model types — analogous to the elementary annuli and convex pieces in the surface case — and prove that such a decomposition exists and is unique.
artifact.status_search_result: A canonical decomposition theorem in higher dimensions has been developed by Choi: for closed real projective n-manifolds he established a canonical decomposition into (n−1)-convex pieces and concave affine pieces (math/9804110, Mémoires SMF 1999), and for closed affine 3-manifolds specifically, "Convex and concave decompositions of affine 3-manifolds" (Bull. Braz. Math. Soc. 2020) proves that such a manifold is either an affine Hopf 3-manifold or decomposes canonically into concave affine submanifolds with incompressible boundary, toral π-submanifolds, and 2-convex affine manifolds. This provides a 3-dimensional analogue, though a decomposition fully parallel to the surface case (purely into "elementary" pieces and properly convex pieces) is not established in the same clean form, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Canonical decomposition of manifolds with flat real projective structure into (n-1)-convex manifolds and concave affine manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: The failure of (n-1)-convexity leads to a natural decomposition of the manifold into simpler real projective manifolds, some of which are (n-1)-convex and others are concave affine.
status_evidence.claim: A canonical decomposition exists in all dimensions n, giving a partial higher-dimensional analogue of the surface case.

status_evidence.title: Convex and Concave Decompositions of Affine 3-Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: A connected closed affine 3-manifold either is an affine Hopf 3-manifold or decomposes canonically to concave affine submanifolds with incompressible boundary, toral π-submanifolds and 2-convex affine manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: A canonical 3-dimensional decomposition theorem has been proved in the affine setting.
